items.originalTitle: Senior SWE-Bench: open-source benchmark that assesses agents as senior engineers
items.summary:
Senior SWE-Bench is an open-source benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on tasks typical of senior software engineers, featuring realistic, naturally phrased instructions and challenges that require runtime debugging and investigation. Unlike traditional benchmarks with over-specified requirements, Senior SWE-Bench tasks simulate real-world scenarios where engineers must interpret under-specified instructions and solve complex bugs using behavioral reports and runtime data.

The benchmark includes multi-phase, multi-stack feature tasks sourced from actual pull requests authored by experienced engineers, emphasizing long-horizon problem-solving across multiple services. Performance is assessed not only on correctness but also on code quality and adherence to best practices, with current leading AI models completing senior-level tasks successfully less than 25% of the time, highlighting the difficulty and realism of the benchmark.

items.originalTitle: Show HN: MyWritingTwin: an AI Writing Profile that makes LLMs sound like you
items.summary:
MyWritingTwin has introduced an AI writing profile that captures an individual's unique writing style for use across various large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. This tool addresses the common issue of AI-generated drafts not matching a user's personal tone and style, which often requires extensive editing. By analyzing over 50 style markers through a seven-dimension framework, MyWritingTwin creates a personalized writing profile that can be deployed seamlessly across different AI platforms without a monthly fee.

The system uses computational stylometry, a technique from forensic linguistics, to extract unique writing patterns including tone, rhythm, vocabulary, and cultural nuances, supporting multiple languages and contexts. Users can generate a comprehensive style guide and a runtime block optimized for AI deployment, enabling consistent and authentic communication in emails, reports, and other formats. The service also offers a free Writing DNA Snapshot to preview individual writing styles and personality indicators.

MyWritingTwin aims to reduce the time and cognitive effort spent on editing AI outputs by ensuring that AI-generated content sounds like the user, enhancing productivity and maintaining consistency across communications. The platform offers various subscription tiers tailored to different user needs, from single-language professionals to enterprise-level solutions.

items.title: Cloudflare introduces new AI traffic management options for all customers, enabling nuanced control over search, agent, and training bots [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Your site, your rules: new AI traffic options for all customers
items.summary:
Cloudflare has introduced new AI traffic management options for all its customers, allowing website owners to exercise more nuanced control over different types of AI bots accessing their content. This update categorizes AI traffic into three main use cases: Search bots that index content for answering queries, Agent bots that perform real-time tasks on behalf of users, and Training bots that use content to train AI models. The goal is to provide website owners with better tools to protect their content, ensure fair compensation, and manage automated traffic more effectively.

This development follows Cloudflare's initial launch of a one-click "Block AI Bots" option and a Pay-Per-Crawl marketplace, which addressed concerns about AI training bots using content without compensation. Recognizing that a one-size-fits-all blocking approach is insufficient, Cloudflare's new taxonomy encourages bot operators to separate their crawlers by purpose, enhancing transparency and control for site owners. These changes reflect the evolving nature of AI-driven web traffic and aim to balance content protection with discoverability and fair use.

items.summary:
Ghbrk is a credential broker designed for AI coding agents running on Linux, enabling them to execute Git and GitHub CLI commands without exposing sensitive SSH keys or API tokens. It operates as a daemon that securely holds credentials and enforces user-defined policies to control and log every remote operation, ensuring that agents never directly access private keys or tokens.

The tool targets autonomous AI coding assistants and bots that interact with GitHub, addressing security risks where agents might inadvertently expose credentials by reading SSH configurations or environment variables. Ghbrk requires explicit calls for remote operations, checks permissions against a root-owned YAML policy file, and logs all decisions to an append-only audit log, providing a controlled and auditable environment for credential use.

items.summary:
AIIT-THRESHOLD, an independent AI-safety research initiative, has released Tessera 1B, an open-source language model with approximately 1 billion parameters. Trained from scratch on a carefully curated corpus of 24.5 billion tokens for just $315, Tessera 1B is designed as a clean, foundational model that produces fluent English and some Japanese but has limited reasoning and factual accuracy. It is intended as a base for further fine-tuning rather than a ready-to-use chat assistant or reasoning system.

The model includes two fine-tuned adapters that offer different conversational tones, both evaluated for safety and coherence. Tessera 1B's training data consists solely of web, books, and academic texts, avoiding synthetic reasoning traces or conversation transcripts to maintain data integrity. The model and its training data are openly licensed, with full provenance provided, supporting transparency and further development by the AI community.

items.originalTitle: Text AI watermarks will always be trivial to remove
items.summary:
The European Union AI Act, enforceable from August 2026, mandates that all AI-generated text must be detectable through watermarks. Despite this requirement, experts highlight that watermarking text remains a challenging problem due to the compressed nature of language and the difficulty of embedding hidden signatures without degrading output quality. Techniques like Google's SynthID offer partial solutions by subtly influencing token selection patterns to create detectable watermarks, but these methods can be fragile and costly to verify.

Text watermarking differs significantly from image watermarking because even minor alterations in text are noticeable, making it hard to conceal watermarks effectively. Some AI providers use strategies that embed mathematical patterns in token choices to signal AI origin, but these can be disrupted by slight changes to the text. The EU's requirement will push AI labs to develop practical watermarking approaches, though the balance between detectability, output quality, and verification cost remains a complex challenge.

Additional large-scale data from other sources supports this pattern, showing increased code churn, review times, and instability without corresponding gains in delivery. The research suggests that AI shifts the bottleneck from code generation to verification, requiring new approaches to measuring and managing productivity in software development.

This perspective was echoed by Paul Bakaus, who advocates for a collaborative approach where AI manages routine work but humans retain control over the final output to ensure originality and ownership.

The discussion extended to generative media, where experts noted that AI models reflect the biases and aesthetics of their creators, underscoring the need for human judgment in shaping outputs. Overall, the event highlighted a balanced view that, despite advances in automation, human understanding and agency remain vital in AI development and application.

items.originalSummary:
Financial data companies such as FactSet and Moody’s appear to have made progress reassuring investors that they won’t be replaced by finance-focused AI tools. But investors may have new questions these days around how the uncertainty of AI costs will affect usage of these businesses’ products.

Investors were spooked when Anthropic and others touted AI products for finance and other professions earlier this year. Companies like FactSet, Moody’s, S&P Global and LSEG, which all make money in part by selling information like market data, company financials and risk analytics, were hit by a market selloff.

Stocks have recovered at least partly since then, and the firms made a pretty compelling argument that rising usage of AI tools doesn’t hurt the value of their data. Banks, asset managers and other regulated customers still need licensed, current information that they can easily verify and audit. 

These firms have also added AI features to their products and made data available in formats customers can access through their own AI tools. Overall, they say AI adoption is positive for demand, because an AI agent can consume far more data than any human analyst. 

But things aren’t proving quite that simple. In recent months, businesses have become more focused on the rising cost of AI usage and many companies are adopting measures to keep AI spending under control. That’s raising a fresh set of AI-related questions for data sellers. 

A big question is who pays the cost of the tokens needed to run AI-powered data analysis. The answer depends on how the access to the data is structured, and whether a customer is using the data through their own AI tools or not. How much more customers are willing to pay for AI to run data analysis is another question. And like AI costs themselves, data consumption by AI tools can be unpredictable, because an agent might rerun queries or try lots of data sets. The overall picture might be unnerving for investors in a business where they’ve long prized relatively steady revenue streams. 

On Wednesday, FactSet CFO Joshua Warren said AI tokens “were not a line item that we really thought about in 2025.” Those costs are showing up in FactSet’s own spending as it uses AI internally and builds AI-powered products for customers. FactSet says it has internal controls like budgeting and model routing, and a recently expanded Google partnership gave it preferential token pricing.

When it comes to customer demand, FactSet executives noted that AI products were proving to be a source of growth and commanding richer contracts, but they also said customers are still not clear on what their own consumption will be, so want flexibility in pricing. 

“In an AI world, right now, there is a lot of value that clients are placing on that,” FactSet CEO Sanoke Viswanathan said, and the company is adding provisions for “new consumption patterns” as customers experiment.

Moody’s, for its part, appeared to be getting ahead of both sides of the cost question. In a June investor Q&A with a JPMorgan research analyst, a Moody’s executive noted that customers bear the AI token costs when they use its data through tools like Claude Enterprise, ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot. They added that Moody’s can help customers keep a lid on those costs, including by packaging its data with instructions that help AI agents use it quickly and efficiently. Moody’s also builds token costs into contracts with customers that are using its own AI tools, but it says it closely monitors those costs through routing and other measures.

To be sure, there isn’t much evidence yet that AI has moved the needle either way. Financial data businesses aren’t exactly blockbuster growth stories, but their recent growth rates still look broadly similar to before the AI scare. 

If anything, the most noticeable impact from the AI boom might be outside these companies’ data subscriptions. LSEG, which also owns the London Stock Exchange and other markets businesses, has suggested that AI is accelerating decision making and activity in general, which translates into more trading activity and risk management needs. Markets revenue jumped in the first quarter, helped by strong trading volumes. 

Meanwhile Moody’s and S&P Global have both said that a surge in debt issuance tied to AI infrastructure spending has boosted their credit ratings businesses, which make money in part when companies issue new debt and pay to have it rated.

The next question is how far into finance these companies can reach with their AI businesses. FactSet executives said on Wednesday that the wealth management industry is still in the early stages of AI adoption, but financial advisers present a big potential customer pool. That could also turn into client-facing tools for people using wealth and consumer financial services. 

New types of users could well have a very different take on AI costs and payoffs than the big existing financial customers, which could introduce further complications around fees and pricing. Meanwhile, the rest of the financial data crowd are due to report results in the coming weeks. We’ll see how the narrative continues to change.

items.summary:
Australian startup Springboards has developed Flint, a large language model (LLM) designed to generate more diverse and creative responses than mainstream models like ChatGPT and Claude. Flint aims to overcome the common issue of groupthink in LLMs, where models tend to produce similar, predictable answers, limiting creativity especially in open-ended tasks such as brainstorming or travel planning.

Springboards' cofounders demonstrated Flint's ability to provide varied responses, such as different random numbers or unique taglines, contrasting with the repetitive outputs of other models. This approach embraces a degree of hallucination to foster novelty, addressing findings from recent research that highlighted the homogeneity of responses across many LLMs trained on similar data. Springboards also offers a tool that integrates Flint alongside other models to help creative professionals generate a wider range of ideas.

items.summary:
Cloudflare has announced a new policy requiring AI companies to separate their web crawlers used for traditional search from those used for AI training and agents by September 15, 2026. If companies fail to comply, their mixed-use crawlers will be blocked by default on many ad-hosting publisher sites. This change aims to give website owners more control over how their content is accessed and used, particularly to protect intellectual property from being freely exploited by AI models.

The policy will affect new and existing Cloudflare customers, especially those using free plans, and reflects a broader shift as bot traffic surpasses human traffic online. Cloudflare is also introducing tools to help publishers monetize AI access to their content, including partnerships with AI companies like Ceramic.ai and You.com. These measures seek to create a more sustainable ecosystem by encouraging transparency and fair compensation for content usage in AI applications.

Cloudflare is also introducing tools to help publishers monetize AI access to their content, including partnerships with AI companies like Ceramic.ai and You.com. These measures seek to create a more sustainable ecosystem by encouraging transparency and fair compensation for content usage in AI applications.

items.originalTitle: Customer Support Tickets That Code
items.summary:
Semgrep, an AI cybersecurity startup, is using Anthropic's Claude AI model to automate the process of converting customer support tickets into code fixes and new features. The AI handles coding tasks in a sandboxed environment, after which human engineers test and integrate the changes into Semgrep's main application, which helps developers identify bugs and vulnerabilities. Currently, this system processes a few tickets per month, with plans to increase its usage.

This approach streamlines the traditionally slow and manual workflow of addressing customer complaints and feature requests by directly linking support tickets to code development. Semgrep's founder, Isaac Evans, highlighted that the integration of AI in this manner could significantly accelerate the response time to customer needs and improve software maintenance efficiency.

items.originalSummary:
Software developers are starting to combine the two most successful uses of large language models: coding and customer support.

Specifically, they’re using AI to automate the process of turning customer complaints about software issues or feature requests into new code. Previously, that could be a long and tedious process, which involved sending customer support tickets to a company’s support team, directing those issues to the relevant engineer, and coding up and testing a fix to the issue. 

AI cybersecurity startup Semgrep, for instance, routes customer complaints about bugs in its app or requests for new features to Anthropic’s Claude model, founder and CEO Isaac Evans said. Claude handles the fix or codes the new features in a sandboxed, isolated version of Semgrep’s app. After a human engineer tests the changes, Semgrep merges them into the real Semgrep app, which primarily helps developers scan their code for bugs and vulnerabilities, he said. Right now, Semgrep is using this approach for a handful of customer support tickets per month, but Evans expects that number to grow quickly, he said.

It is positioned as an upgrade over the previous Nano Banana model, optimized for speed and efficiency. Gemini Omni Flash enables developers to create and edit videos interactively, combining text, image, and video inputs to maintain scene consistency and apply real-world knowledge. This release aims to facilitate creative iteration and comprehensive multimedia experiences for developers and users alike.

items.originalTitle: Claude Science is Anthropic’s newest flagship product
items.summary:
Anthropic has launched Claude Science, a standalone AI product designed to support scientific research and drug development, now available to all paid Claude subscribers. The product aims to assist researchers by autonomously performing complex tasks based on high-level instructions, with specialized tools for computational biology and drug discovery. This launch marks a significant step for Anthropic, placing Claude Science alongside its other flagship AI products like Claude Code and Claude Cowork.

Claude Science builds on Anthropic's previous efforts in AI for life sciences, offering enhanced capabilities such as running code on powerful computer clusters and ensuring reproducibility of scientific results. The tool is particularly focused on molecular and cellular biology applications and demonstrated its potential by identifying new drug candidates for rare diseases. Anthropic will also use Claude Science for its own research into treatments for neglected diseases, highlighting the company's commitment to advancing AI-driven scientific discovery.
